primer.title: Why data delivery is changing
primer.body:
Each generation of data delivery changed who does the work and where the logic lives. The AI-native lifecycle keeps the warehouse disciplines (conformed dimensions, SCD history, reconciliation) and changes the executor.

| Dimension | Appliance EDW + ETL tool | Cloud ELT (dbt era) | AI-assisted data engineering | AI-native data delivery on Snowflake |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Core philosophy | Central warehouse, GUI mappings (ODI, Informatica), nightly batch. | SQL-first transformations in version control, cloud warehouse elasticity. | Engineers write SQL faster with copilots; same process. | Intent and context drive agents that profile, convert, build, test and reconcile; people own the gates. |
| Primary executor | ETL developer and DBA. | Analytics engineer. | Analytics engineer accepting inline suggestions. | Agents (Cortex Code, Claude Code, Niche Accelerate services) supervised by AI-native engineers. |
| Unit of work | Mapping, stored procedure, report. | dbt model, test, exposure. | Prompt, snippet, single model. | PRD, solution design, scope.yaml, component change spec, data product spec. |
| Migration approach | Manual rewrite, spreadsheet mapping. | Lift and shift, then refactor. | Copilot-assisted rewrite. | SnowConvert AI and AIM convert; agents handle the residue; every object reconciled before cut-over. |
| Quality | End-of-project UAT, manual spot checks. | dbt tests, CI. | Generated test stubs. | Generated unit, reconciliation, RLS and performance tests run every sprint; reconciliation ledger per wave. |
| Where business logic lives | RPDs, ETL tools, report calculations, spreadsheets. | dbt models plus BI tools. | Same as before. | One certified semantic layer (semantic views) that grounds dashboards, Cortex Analyst and agents alike. |
| Human judgment | Everything. | Modeling, review, release. | Review of suggestions. | Intent, KPI definitions, architecture and security, gate approvals, variance sign-off. |

The shift: AI stops being a faster keyboard and becomes part of a governed delivery system. On Snowflake that system is unusually complete: conversion (SnowConvert AI, AIM), governance (Horizon), semantics (Semantic Views) and AI (Cortex) all sit where the data lives.
primer.summary: From hand-built ETL and appliance warehouses, to cloud ELT, to AI-assisted SQL, and now to agent-orchestrated data delivery on Snowflake.

primer.title: The six mindset shifts
primer.body:
Move from "what SQL do I need to write?" to "what trusted outcome do I need, and how do I design the people and agent system that produces it?"
### 1. From pipelines to data products
Describe the data product once (grain, owners, quality rules, masking) and let the Data Harness compile Bronze, Silver and Gold, tests, lineage and the schedule.
### 2. From writing SQL to engineering intent
Effort moves to specifying grain, conformed dimensions, SCD behaviour, freshness SLAs and acceptance criteria that an agent can verify before raising a pull request.
### 3. From documentation to semantic context
Lineage in Horizon, certified KPI definitions in semantic views, SOPs in Cortex Search and ADRs in the repo are the context agents read at the point of work.
### 4. From migration to reconciled migration
Conversion is cheap now; trust is not. Success is every measure matching legacy, or the variance explained and signed off, before a report is switched.
### 5. From reports to questions
Design starts with persona questions (what happened, why, what will happen, what to do) and works back to dashboards, Cortex Analyst and agents on the same certified metrics.
### 6. From individual to pod productivity
Measure the pod: conversion rate, reconciliation pass rate, first-pass acceptance and time from PRD to verified-in-production, not lines of SQL accepted.
primer.summary: Six shifts: pipelines to data products, SQL to intent, documentation to semantic context, migration to reconciled migration, reports to questions, and individual to pod productivity.

primer.title: What changes and what does not
primer.body:
### Stays human
- Accountability for every number a business user or customer sees
- KPI definitions and the named KPI arbiter when teams disagree
- Architecture: medallion design, conformed dimensions, security model
- Compliance decisions: SOX or HIPAA controls, Snowflake edition, masking rules approved by data owners
- Go / no-go for cut-over and legacy decommissioning
- Code ownership: the client owns every model, script and document
### Changes fundamentally
- Execution: agents convert DDL, procedures and ETL, and draft dbt models, tests and semantic views
- Discovery: estate scans and lineage are generated, not interviewed into spreadsheets
- Quality: reconciliation and RLS tests are generated and run every sprint
- BI: report logic is extracted and normalized into one semantic layer
- Team shape: a small AI Native core pod builds frameworks; AI-Assisted track pods apply them per wave
- Economics: effort follows unit models with explicit AI speed-up, validated in the pilot
### Accountability in an agentic world
An agent can convert 300 procedures overnight. It does not sign off a reconciliation variance, approve masking on payroll data or decide to switch off Oracle. Those decisions sit with named people at G1, G2 and G3, and in the steering forum.
primer.summary: What stays with people, what changes fundamentally, and who answers for a number when an agent built the pipeline.

primer.title: The data engineering mental model
primer.body:
Intent→Context→Agents→Snowflake tools→Evaluation→Human gate→Trusted outcome

| Component | On a Snowflake program | Human role | Agent role |
|---|---|---|---|
| Intent | PRD per wave: personas, questions, KPIs, grain, freshness, NFRs (filters under 5 s). | Product owner states outcomes and numeric targets; signs G1. | PRD Agent drafts from one prompt and clarifying questions. |
| Context | Legacy lineage, ODI or Informatica repository, OAC RPD, KPI dictionary, data classification, ADRs. | Curates authoritative sources; resolves conflicts. | Estate Analyzer and Horizon catalog index and summarize. |
| Agents | Code Converter, Zone Mapper, RBAC Designer, Report Converter, ETL Test Agent, Promotion Agent. | Selects and supervises; invokes skills by hand. | Multi-step conversion, generation and testing; raises pull requests. |
| Snowflake tools | SnowConvert AI, AIM, Cortex Code, dbt, schemachange, Terraform, Snowpipe, dynamic tables. | Configures access, warehouses and policies. | Calls tools through CLI, MCP and APIs. |
| Evaluation | Reconciliation ledger, dbt tests, SCD checks, RLS tests, golden queries, performance at production volume. | Defines thresholds and the evidence standard. | Generates, runs and triages tests. |
| Human gate | G1 PRD approved · G2 solution design approved · G3 verified in production. | Approves, rejects or signs off variance. | Presents evidence packs and change summaries. |
| Outcome | Legacy retired on date, certified KPIs, AI-ready Gold layer. | Owns the business value. | Delivers the work product for review. |
primer.summary: Intent, context, agents, Snowflake tools, evaluation, human gate and outcome: what people and agents each do.

primer.title: From AI user to AI-native data engineer
primer.body:
| Role | What they do on a Snowflake program | Typical pod |
|---|---|---|
| AI-assisted engineer | Uses Cortex Code or Copilot inline to write SQL and dbt faster. | Track pod (entry) |
| Agent-assisted engineer | Hands bounded tasks to skills: /convert-ddl, /gen-unit-tests, /reconcile, /compare-reports. | Track pod |
| Agent orchestrator | Runs a wave end to end: conversion, ingestion, Gold models and dashboards through the Build Agents. | Track pod lead |
| AI-native data engineer | Builds and adapts Niche Accelerate services, skills and harnesses; tunes conversion rates in the pilot. | Core pod (often partner-funded) |
| AI-native data architect | Owns medallion, semantic layer, security model and the guardrails agents run inside. | Core pod |
| AI-native delivery lead | Manages human and agent capacity, unit effort, gate throughput and credit spend. | Core pod |
| AI program manager | Runs the integrated plan back from licence dates, RAID with integration and platform vendors, steering. | Delivery leadership |

FlyHigh shape: Core pod (AI Native: solution architect, BI analyst, program manager, senior data engineer, testing lead, DevOps) plus two AI-Assisted track pods (senior data engineer, BI engineer, QA, DevOps). Peak 12 FTE plus 3 Niche-funded AI engineers, with a Snowflake architect, AI engineering SME, logistics domain architect and Tableau expert on demand.
primer.summary: Seven roles along the maturity curve, and how they staff an AI Native core pod and AI-Assisted track pods.

primer.title: What good looks like
primer.body:
### Good intent
PRDs with personas, questions, KPI targets, grain and freshness that an agent can test against.
### Good context
Lineage, KPI dictionary, classification and ADRs current and in the repo or Horizon, not in someone's head.
### Good agents
Narrow roles (converter, reconciler, promoter) with only the roles and warehouses they need.
### Good orchestration
Staggered waves (build, SIT, UAT one month apart) so pods keep moving while gates are reviewed.
### Good evaluation
Reconciliation, RLS and performance tests generated and run every sprint, with a ledger of results.
### Good human intervention
People spend time on KPI conflicts, variances, masking and go / no-go, not on boilerplate DDL.
The result: legacy retired on the licence date, 100% of measures reconciled or signed off, filters under 5 seconds on live data, 90%+ of committed stories accepted at show-and-tell, and a Gold layer ready for Cortex.
primer.summary: Six qualities of high-performing AI-native data delivery and the measures that prove them.

primer.title: Where it applies on Snowflake
primer.body:
**Archetype 1**
### Legacy warehouse migration
Oracle ADW, Netezza, Teradata, Greenplum, SQL Server to Snowflake with SnowConvert AI, AIM and Niche Accelerate Platform Migration; ETL tools to dbt and Snowpipe.
**Archetype 2**
### Data products and medallion build
POCs, point-to-point feeds and new sources rebuilt as governed Bronze, Silver and Gold data products with the Data Harness.
**Archetype 3**
### BI and semantic modernization
OAC, Power BI, Cognos, Qlik, MicroStrategy and Klipfolio to Tableau Cloud or Power BI on live Snowflake connections and one semantic layer.
**Archetype 4**
### Cortex AI and agents
Cortex Analyst, Search and Agents on certified semantic views; AI functions in pipelines; Snowflake Intelligence for executives and customers.
Across all
### Platform run and FinOps
Resource monitors, query insights and Cortex Code for run support, with incident and cost reviews after go-live.
primer.summary: Migration, data products, BI and semantics, Cortex AI and agents, and platform run with FinOps.

practices.title: Rationalize before you migrate
practices.detail: Decide keep, merge, rebuild or retire for every report before its wave. About 400 reports rarely means 400 builds.

practices.title: Reconcile every measure
practices.detail: Row counts and measures match legacy, or the variance is explained and signed off. Keep a reconciliation ledger per wave.

practices.title: Like for like first, then improve
practices.detail: Keep layouts so users compare numbers, not designs. Redesign comes after trust, or as a change request.

practices.title: Prove the conversion rate in the pilot
practices.detail: Estimates assume high automated conversion. Profile the estate, run the pilot, then reset wave unit effort from evidence.

practices.title: Plan back from licence dates
practices.detail: Sequence waves from renewal dates; start the parallel run by month 5; allow 30–45 days of business change lead time.

practices.title: Certify KPIs once, with an arbiter
practices.detail: One owner, grain, source fact and golden query per KPI, published as a semantic view that dashboards and Cortex share.

practices.title: Keep history off the integration tool
practices.detail: Move terabyte-scale history with DMS or bulk unload to S3; keep the integration platform for incremental loads.

practices.title: Secure from day one
practices.detail: Masking, row access and SSO in the foundation, not after UAT. Decide the Snowflake edition early when SOX or HIPAA apply.

practices.title: Humans own three gates
practices.detail: G1 PRD, G2 design, G3 verified in production, with a 5-business-day review SLA. Decompose needs no gate.

practices.title: FinOps from the first sprint
practices.detail: Resource monitors, workload warehouses and cost per workload reviewed at every steering, including agent spend.
